diagnostic_evidence.quote: The exponent vectors are stored in sparse form (e.g.\ hash maps or compressed index-value arrays)
The DCR construction scales linearly with spin ($\mathcal{O}(j)$).

issues.failure_explanation: Storing every ratio as an explicit sparse exponent vector requires superlinear storage even for symmetric 6j-symbols. After correcting the recurrence, write z=3j+t. Every divisor d>2 of t+1 contributes a nonzero entry from the denominator [t+1]^4: complete cancellation would require d to divide both j+1 and 3j+1, hence d to divide 2. Consequently the stored sequence has at least sum_{n<=j}(tau(n)-2)=Omega(j log j) entries. This defect survives correction of the recurrence.

Preserving strict linear storage would require an implicit or shared representation of the updates rather than the stated collection of explicit sparse vectors.
issues.overall_effect: The strict O(j) compilation-memory claims are incompatible with the specified explicit sparse representation; finite memory measurements do not establish that asymptotic rate.
issues.title: Explicit sparse ratio storage is not linear in spin
issues.why_classification: A limited logarithmic weakening preserves the main advantage over dense representations, but the advertised memory rate cannot be retained by a routine textual correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We also track the intrinsic condition number ($\log_{10}\kappa$), which dictates the absolute theoretical minimum for precision loss.

issues.failure_explanation: This condition number measures worst-case sensitivity to independent relative perturbations of the summands; it is not a lower bound on the error of every computation. At q=1, the permitted two-term factorial-ratio sum M-(M-1)=1 has kappa=2M-1. For representable integers M=2^m in the double-precision integer range, both terms and their subtraction can be exact despite arbitrarily large kappa within that range.

failure_location.quote: Even perfectly implemented floating-point algorithms cannot avoid precision loss once $\kappa$ becomes large.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe log10(kappa) as a worst-case precision budget or sensitivity indicator, and remove claims that it is an absolute lower bound on attained numerical accuracy.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted mandatory digit loss and the inference that observed residual error proves exhaustion of all representation-level improvements are unsupported.
issues.title: The condition number is incorrectly treated as an unavoidable error lower bound

diagnostic_evidence.quote: yielding an efficient and numerically stable evaluation pipeline, particularly near the unit circle
Consequently, the DCR achieves near-optimal scaling with respect to summation length and approaches the minimal error dictated by the intrinsic conditioning of the problem.

issues.failure_explanation: Numerator and denominator magnitudes do not bound errors in evaluating their cyclotomic factors, powers, or recurrences. For example, with q=i+delta and delta^2 comparable to unit roundoff, ordinary evaluation of Phi_2(q^2)=q^2+1 can lose the delta^2 real part and incur relative error of order sqrt(epsilon). A one-term [2]_q has kappa=1 and |gamma_rep| only O(|log epsilon|), so the claimed bound predicts the much smaller O(epsilon |log epsilon|), even if the summation-length convention is repaired. Moreover gamma_rep can be negative and is not a numerical condition measure.
